scope: Review of newly discovered, openly licensed adult-mouse spinal-cord FIB-SEM volumes for a documented exact interneuron-object route and potential source-local ultrastructure comparison.

candidateVolumes.sample: Wild-type female, 6-month-old mouse dorsal corticospinal tract
candidateVolumes.admissionNote: Public raw EM volume. The article reports selected corticospinal-axon ER and mitochondria reconstructions; this is a projection-axon tract comparator, not an interneuron record. No source mask or exact reconstructed-axon ID was imported in this audit.

candidateVolumes.sample: Atl1 KI/KI / Reep1 KO female, 6-month-old mouse dorsal corticospinal tract
candidateVolumes.admissionNote: Public raw EM volume from a disease-model mouse. The published ER morphology is genotype- and disease-context-specific; it is not a normal interneuron template. No source mask or exact reconstructed-axon ID was imported in this audit.

article.title: Transverse endoplasmic reticulum expansion in hereditary spastic paraplegia corticospinal axons
article.reportedManualReconstruction: One selected corticospinal axon per genotype was manually reconstructed across 501 consecutive images; the publication also describes machine-learning-based ER and mitochondria analysis across the FIB-SEM volumes.

admission.interpretation: These open, high-resolution spinal-cord FIB-SEM volumes establish availability of an adjacent mouse spinal ultrastructure reference, not a mouse interneuron volume or interneuron cell identity. They may be used only as separately labeled corticospinal-axon comparators unless a source-supported cell-object crosswalk is found.
